statement: Beads on a string go: 1 black, 1 white, 2 black, 1 white, 3 black, 1 white, and so on. How many beads are there up to and including the 5th white bead?

choices.misconception: I counted only the white beads.
I stopped at the 4th white bead instead of the 5th.
I counted only the black beads, 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5, and left out the white ones.
I stopped just before the 5th white bead, so I left that bead out.

hints: Each white bead ends a group. What is in each group?
Split the string into groups that each end with a white bead. The black beads in each group go up by one. Count the beads in each group, then add up the first five groups.
The groups have 1 + 1, 2 + 1, 3 + 1, 4 + 1 and 5 + 1 beads. That is 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 beads.

solutions.reliable: Each white bead ends a group: group 1 has 1 black and 1 white, group 2 has 2 black and 1 white, and so on. The first five groups have 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6 beads, and 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 + 6 = 20. The idea to keep: split a growing pattern into repeating groups, then count the groups you need.
solutions.elegant: Count the two colours separately: black beads 1 + 2 + 3 + 4 + 5 = 15 and white beads 5, so 15 + 5 = 20.

whyOnTest: Growing patterns hide a group that repeats, and stopping one group early or leaving out the last bead are the common slips.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
